findings.source_passage: getting the face of the poor. Get off, Queequeg! Look, he'll twitch you off soon. I wonder he don't wake.
findings.why_it_matters: The 'grinding the face of the poor' biblical allusion is the sharpest comic-ironic moment in the scene; its omission erases Ishmael's characteristic scriptural wit and the passage's interpretive texture.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'grinding the face of the poor' line verbatim or near-verbatim within the comic exchange about Queequeg sitting on the rigger.

findings.source_passage: the king, chiefs, and great people generally, were in the custom of fattening some of the lower orders for ottomans; and to furnish a house comfortably in that respect, you had only to buy up eight or ten lazy fellows, and lay them round in the piers and alcoves.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Queequeg removed himself to just beyond the head'
findings.why_it_matters: Queequeg's deadpan ethnographic explanation of human ottomans is a signature comic-philosophical digression that establishes the novel's satirical primitivism; its complete omission flattens the scene to mere plot.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the core conceit — fattening the lower orders as ottomans, buying eight or ten lazy fellows — even in compressed paraphrase that preserves the absurdist register.

findings.source_passage: Oh! I was going to warn ye against—but never mind, never mind—it's all one, all in the family too;—sharp frost this morning, ain't it? Good-bye to ye. Shan't see ye again very soon, I guess; unless it's before the Grand Jury.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Morning to ye! morning to ye!'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'Grand Jury' line is one of Elijah's most ominous prophetic gestures; the draft preserves the words but drops 'all one, all in the family too' and other surrounding phrases that give the warning its cumulative foreboding texture.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'never mind—it's all one, all in the family too' before the frost and Grand Jury lines to preserve the full prophetic build.

findings.source_passage: I beat the thing down; and again marking the sleeper, jocularly hinted to Queequeg that perhaps we had best sit up with the body
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Those sailors we saw, Queequeg'
findings.why_it_matters: Ishmael's self-conscious rationalizing ('I beat the thing down') and macabre humor ('sit up with the body') are voice-defining moments that the draft bypasses, slightly dulling the narrator's characteristic ironic self-awareness.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a clause capturing Ishmael's deliberate suppression of doubt and his gallows-humor suggestion to 'sit up with the body'; these need not be verbatim but the psychological texture should survive.

summary: Three medium-severity failures — the 'grinding the face of the poor' biblical irony, the entire human-ottomans digression, and partial flattening of Elijah's prophetic valediction — collectively constitute enough voice erasure to require regeneration.
